  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1682: the leaderboard step commits the updated fa-results
    # ledger + regenerated README table back to the repo.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" \
            --json-summary leaderboard-summary.json jobs

      # gh-1682: auto-update the public leaderboard — append the run's
      # result to bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json (idempotent: keyed by
      # dataset version + model, run URLs union) and regenerate the
      # README table. Runs only on a COMPLETE full run (the verdict step
      # succeeded) — smoke/narrowed dispatches (non-empty tasks) never
      # touch the ledger.
      - name: Update leaderboard ledger & table
        if: success() && inputs.tasks == ''
        env:
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary leaderboard-summary.json
          # No --version: render every ledger version + the 4.0 field,
          # so the marked README block is rewritten whole, never shrunk
          # to the dispatch's single family.
          python bench/leaderboard/render.py
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "leaderboard: ledger and table already up to date"
          else
            git commit -m "bench: leaderboard ledger update · ${FAMILY} · ${MODEL} (gh-1682)"
            git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for the gh-1682 leaderboard tooling.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard

Hermetic: fetch-parse tests run against fixture captures (a real
tbench.ai page and a real Harbor Hub leaderboard-read response, both
captured 2026-10-18); no test touches the network.
"""
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import fetch
import record
import render

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURES = HERE / "fixtures"


def load_json(name: str) -> dict:
    return json.loads((FIXTURES / name).read_text())


class FetchHubParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_hub_fixture_normalizes(self):
        payload = load_json("hub_2-1_main.json")
        doc = fetch.normalize_hub_payload(payload, "2.1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["schema"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(doc["version"], "2.1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["source"], "harbor-hub")
        self.assertEqual(doc["package"], "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["leaderboard"], "main")
        rows = doc["rows"]
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), payload["pagination"]["total"])
        first = rows[0]

    # from other families so merged artifacts never cross-contaminate.
    job_dirs = [d for d in sorted(args.jobs_dir.glob("*")) if d.is_dir()]
    if args.family:
        job_dirs = [d for d in job_dirs if d.name.startswith(f"fa-{args.family}-")]

    splits: dict[str, list[dict]] = {"cpu": [], "gpu": []}
    # gh-1658 C3: readable result.json count per shard index (the job

    shard_trials: dict[int, int] = {}

        if "-gpu-" in name:
            split = "gpu"
        elif "-cpu-" in name:
            split = "cpu"
        else:
            # legacy scheme: docker shards were CPU, modal was the GPU leg
            split = "gpu" if "modal" in name else "cpu"
        rows = _trial_rows(job_dir)
        splits[split].extend(rows)
        index = _shard_index(name)
        if index is not None:
            shard_trials[index] = shard_trials.get(index, 0) + len(rows)

    # test harnesses load this module without the dir on sys.path.
    title = ledger = None
    if args.family:
        import families

        if args.family not in families.FAMILIES:
            # Defense in depth: the workflow resolves the dataset via
            # families.py before dispatch, but a direct summary call must
            # not silently render a mis-keyed report.
            print(
                f"::error::unknown Terminal-Bench family '{args.family}' —"
                f" resolve the dataset id first (families.py resolve);"
                f" known: {', '.join(sorted(families.FAMILIES))}",

            "run_url": args.run_url or "—",

New `bench/leaderboard/` tooling (stdlib-only python, same as the rest of bench/): `fetch.py` normalizes official Terminal-Bench leaderboard rows (model, agent, accuracy, date, source) for a dataset version, `record.py` upserts fa's own results into a committed `fa_results.json` ledger, and `render.py` merges both into a marked README section. # gh-1682: [GOAL] fa leaderboard table: fetch official tbench stats + overlay self-reported fa bench results, auto-updated by bench runs

## Description

### Goal

A visible, auto-updating **fa vs. the field** leaderboard table: pull the official Terminal-Bench stats (tbench.ai, `?version=2.1` today — Next.js app, data embedded in page JSON / backed by the Harbor hub API per docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/leaderboards), overlay fa's own bench results (we ran TB 2.0 earlier and 2.1 now), render a polished table for users.

### Design sketch (to be refined in implementation)

1. **Fetcher** (`bench/leaderboard/` script, python — same tooling as the rest of bench tooling): pull the official leaderboard rows for a given dataset version (2.0 / 2.1 / later 3.0/4.0 when they stabilize). Source of truth preference: Harbor hub API if it exposes leaderboard rows; fallback: parse tbench.ai's embedded page JSON. Never scrape HTML tables by regex — the page is Next.js with embedded structured data.
2. **fa rows source**: our own bench-harbor run summaries (`harbor-jobs-merged` artifact → summary.py accuracy) keyed by (dataset version, model, fa version, run url). A small committed ledger file (e.g. `bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json`) appended by the bench workflow on every completed run — that's the auto-update hook.
3. **Renderer**: Markdown table into `README.md` (between markers) and/or `docs/leaderboard.md` — rank by accuracy, fa rows highlighted. Honesty contract: fa rows are **self-reported, not on the official leaderboard** (community submissions are closed for 2.1/3.0/4.0 — see #1681) and must render with a visible marker + footnote (run date, fa version, dataset version, link to the GH run). Never blend self-reported rows visually with official rows.
4. **Auto-update**: bench-harbor.yml aggregate step appends the run's result to the ledger and regenerates the table (same commit as the run artifacts flow), so the table refreshes on every bench completion. Manual regeneration script for backfills.

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench/leaderboard/fetch.py --version 2.1` produces a normalized JSON of official rows (model, agent, accuracy, date, source url).
2. `fa_results.json` ledger + renderer: README section with the merged table, fa rows marked self-reported with run links.
3. bench-harbor.yml appends + re-renders on run completion (idempotent; a re-run of the same job updates, not duplicates).
4. Unit tests for fetch-parse (fixture HTML/JSON captured from tbench.ai) and merge/render logic.

### Context

- Official submissions are closed for TB 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 at the time of writing — this table is our public-facing evidence until #1681 (hub upload + ATIF) lets us submit officially.
- Latest fa numbers to seed the ledger: TB 2.1 kimi-for-coding 300/445 = 67.4% (runs 39028127116 + 39052822079 + 39098996789), GLM-5.3-flash 257/445 = 57.8% (run 38823577512).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Official Terminal-Bench leaderboard fetcher (gh-1682).

Usage:
    fetch.py --version 2.1 [--out rows.json] [--source auto|hub|tbench]

Pulls the official leaderboard rows for one Terminal-Bench dataset
version and prints a normalized JSON document:

    {
      "schema": 1,
      "version": "2.1",
      "package": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1",
      "leaderboard": "main",
      "title": "Terminal-Bench 2.1",
      "source": "harbor-hub" | "tbench.ai",
      "fetched_at": "<iso8601>",
      "rows": [
        {"rank": 1, "agent": "Codex", "agent_url": ...,
         "model": "GPT-6 Astra", "model_url": ...,
         "accuracy": 87.42, "n_trials": 445, "date": "2026-09-03",
         "cost_usd": ...},
        ...
      ]
    }

Source of truth (ticket order): the Harbor Hub API first — the public
`leaderboard-read` function documented at
docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/leaderboards and backing tbench.ai.
Fallback: parse tbench.ai's embedded page JSON (a Next.js app — the
leaderboard dehydrates into `self.__next_f.push` RSC payloads). HTML
tables are NEVER regex-scraped; only the embedded structured JSON is
read. `--source tbench` forces the fallback (used by tests/backfills).

Version -> (package, leaderboard name), verified live against the Hub
on 2026-10-18: the 2.x boards live under their own packages (only the
4.x/3.x generations share `terminal-bench/terminal-bench`):

    2.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2    2-0
    2.1  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1  main
    3.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      3-0-0
    4.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      4-0-0

Stdlib only (same tooling constraint as the rest of bench/).
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# version label -> (hub package, leaderboard name). Verified live against
# the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function (gh-1682).
BOARDS = {
    "2.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2", "2-0"),
    "2.1": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1", "main"),
    "3.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "3-0-0"),
    "4.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "4-0-0"),
}

HUB_READ_URL = "https://api.harborframework.com/functions/v1/leaderboard-read"
TBENCH_URL = "https://www.tbench.ai/"
# Hub row lists are paged; the docs example uses 100 and tbench.ai's own
# boards are a few dozen rows, so one page of 1000 covers a board whole.
HUB_PAGE_SIZE = 1000
HUB_MAX_PAGES = 20
HTTP_TIMEOUT = 30
USER_AGENT = "fa-leaderboard-fetch (gh-1682)"

# HTML tables are never scraped — only the Next.js RSC payload lines.
_RSC_PUSH_RE = re.compile(
    r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[1,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*\]\)'
)


def board_for(version: str) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    """Resolve a version label (or a bare board name under the 4.x
    package) to its (package, name); unknown versions fail loudly."""
    if version in BOARDS:
        return BOARDS[version]
    raise SystemExit(
        f"error: unknown Terminal-Bench version '{version}' — known boards: "
        + ", ".join(sorted(BOARDS))
    )


def _label(value) -> str:
    """Hub metadata fields are {'label': ..., 'url': ...} objects (or
    plain strings in older rows) — the table wants the label."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("label")
    return value


def _url(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("url")
    return None


def normalize_hub_payload(payload: dict, version: str) -> dict:
    """Normalize a leaderboard-read response body into our row schema."""
    lb = payload.get("leaderboard") or {}
    rows = []
    for row in payload.get("rows") or []:
        md = row.get("metadata") or {}
        mt = row.get("metrics") or {}
        rows.append(
            {
                "rank": row.get("rank"),
                "agent": _label(md.get("agent_display")),
                "agent_url": _url(md.get("agent_display")),
                "model": _label(md.get("model_display")),
                "model_url": _url(md.get("model_display")),
                "accuracy": mt.get("accuracy"),
                "n_trials": mt.get("n_trials"),
                "date": md.get("date"),
                "cost_usd": mt.get("total_cost_usd"),
            }
        )
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["accuracy"] is None, -(r["accuracy"] or 0)))
    return {
        "schema": 1,
        "version": version,
        "package": lb.get("package"),
        "leaderboard": lb.get("name"),
        "title": lb.get("title"),
        "source": "harbor-hub",
        "source_url": HUB_READ_URL,
        "fetched_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "rows": rows,
    }


def parse_tbench_page(html: str, package: str, name: str) -> list:
    """Extract one leaderboard's dehydrated rows from a tbench.ai page.

    tbench.ai is a Next.js app: the leaderboard query result dehydrates
    into `self.__next_f.push([1,"<json>"])` lines. We decode every such
    payload, find the query whose key is ["leaderboard", package, name],
    and return its data rows. Returns [] when the page does not carry
    that board (never an HTML-table fallback).
    """
    for raw in _RSC_PUSH_RE.findall(html):
        # The captured group is a JSON string literal — json.loads
        # decodes both \" and \uXXXX correctly (unicode_escape would
        # mangle multi-byte labels).
        try:
            text = json.loads('"' + raw + '"')
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        start = text.find("{")
        if start < 0:
            continue
        try:
            payload, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[start:])
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        queries = (payload.get("state") or {}).get("queries") or []
        for query in queries:
            if query.get("queryKey") != ["leaderboard", package, name]:
                continue
            data = (query.get("state") or {}).get("data") or {}
            return list(data.get("rows") or [])
    return []


def normalize_tbench_rows(rows: list, version: str, package: str,
                          name: str, title: str = None) -> dict:
    """Normalize tbench.ai RSC rows — same shape as the Hub rows."""
    doc = normalize_hub_payload(
        {"leaderboard": {"package": package, "name": name, "title": title},
         "rows": rows},
        version,
    )
    doc["source"] = "tbench.ai"
    doc["source_url"] = TBENCH_URL
    return doc


def _http_json(url: str, payload: dict = None) -> dict:
    data = None
    headers = {"User-Agent": USER_AGENT, "Accept": "application/json"}
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())


def _http_get(url: str) -> str:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return resp.read().decode()


def fetch_hub(version: str) -> dict:
    """Read a board through the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function,
    paging through total_pages."""
    package, name = board_for(version)
    rows = []
    title = None
    got_package = package
    for page in range(1, HUB_MAX_PAGES + 1):
        payload = _http_json(
            HUB_READ_URL,
            {"package": package, "name": name, "page": page,
             "page_size": HUB_PAGE_SIZE},
        )
        lb = payload.get("leaderboard") or {}
        title = lb.get("title") or title
        got_package = lb.get("package") or got_package
        rows.extend(payload.get("rows") or [])
        pagination = payload.get("pagination") or {}
        if page >= pagination.get("total_pages", 1):
            break
    return normalize_hub_payload(
        {"leaderboard": {"package": got_package, "name": name,
                         "title": title},
         "rows": rows},
        version,
    )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Leaderboard renderer: merge official rows + fa self-reported rows into
the README table (gh-1682).

Usage:
    render.py [--version 2.1]... [--top 15] [--offline] [--readme README.md]

Renders one subsection per dataset version into the marked region of
README.md:

    <!-- leaderboard:begin -->
    ...generated...
    <!-- leaderboard:end -->

Honesty contract (gh-1682 AC2): official rows and fa rows live in
SEPARATE tables under separate headers — fa rows carry a ⭐ marker, the
"self-reported, not on the official leaderboard" label, and a footnote
with run date, fa version, dataset version, and the GitHub run link(s).
They are never sorted into or styled like official rows.

Official rows come from fetch.py (Harbor Hub API -> tbench.ai page-JSON
fallback). `--offline` reads the committed snapshots instead — the
snapshots keep README regeneration reproducible and let the auto-update
step degrade to the last captured board instead of failing when the hub
is unreachable. A version with no official rows and no snapshot renders
an explicit "no official rows" note — never an empty table that could
read as an empty field.

Regenerating with unchanged inputs leaves README.md untouched (the
workflow's commit step relies on that for idempotency).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import fetch
import record

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
README_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "README.md"
SNAPSHOT_DIR = HERE / "snapshots"

MARKER_BEGIN = "<!-- leaderboard:begin (gh-1682) -->"
MARKER_END = "<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->"
INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING = "## What's inside"
# README section header lives inside the marked region, so removing the
# markers removes the whole section.
SECTION_HEADER = "## Leaderboard: fa vs. the field"
FA_MARKER = "⭐"

DEFAULT_OFFICIAL_VERSIONS = ("4.0",)


def pct(part: int, total: int) -> str:
    return f"{100.0 * part / total:.1f}%" if total else "n/a"


def _link(label: str, url: str) -> str:
    return f"[{label}]({url})" if url else label


def _run_link(url: str) -> str:
    """A GitHub Actions run URL renders by its run id (the stable,
    auditable handle) — full URLs in every cell would drown the table."""
    run_id = url.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return _link(run_id, url)


def render_official_table(doc: dict, top: int) -> "list[str]":
    rows = doc.get("rows") or []
    shown = rows[:top]
    lines = [
        "| # | Agent | Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for i, r in enumerate(shown, 1):
        lines.append(
            "| {rank} | {agent} | {model} | {acc} | {n} | {date} |".format(
                rank=r.get("rank") or i,
                agent=_link(r["agent"], r.get("agent_url")) or "—",
                model=_link(r["model"], r.get("model_url")) or "—",
                acc=pct_1(r.get("accuracy")),
                n=r.get("n_trials") or "—",
                date=r.get("date") or "—",
            )
        )
    fetched = (doc.get("fetched_at") or "")[:10]
    note = (
        f"Official rows: Harbor Hub leaderboard "
        f"`{doc.get('package')}/{doc.get('leaderboard')}` — "
        f"backing [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/)"
    )
    if len(rows) > len(shown):
        note += f", top {len(shown)} of {len(rows)}"
    if fetched:
        note += f", fetched {fetched}"
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"<sub>{note}.</sub>")
    return lines


def pct_1(accuracy) -> str:
    """Hub accuracy is a 0-100 percentage; render one decimal."""
    if accuracy is None:
        return "n/a"
    return f"{float(accuracy):.1f}%"


def render_fa_table(rows: "list[dict]", version: str) -> "list[str]":
    lines = [
        "| Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date | fa | Runs |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in rows:
        runs = " + ".join(_run_link(u) for u in r.get("run_urls") or []) or "—"
        fa = r.get("fa_version") or "—"
        lines.append(
            f"| {FA_MARKER} {r.get('model', '—')} "
            f"| {pct(r.get('resolved', 0), r.get('total', 0))} "
            f"| {r.get('resolved', '—')}/{r.get('total', '—')} "
            f"| {r.get('date', '—')} "
            f"| `{fa}` "
            f"| {runs} |"
        )
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        f"<sub>{FA_MARKER} Self-reported: measured by our own "
        f"`bench-harbor` runs on Terminal-Bench {version}, **not** an "
        "official leaderboard submission (community submissions are "
        "closed — #1681). Every row links its GitHub Actions run(s); fa "
        "rows never blend into the official table above. Source: "
        "`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json`.</sub>"
    )
    return lines


def render_version_section(version: str, official: dict,
                           fa_rows: "list[dict]", top: int,
                           offline_note: bool) -> str:
    title = (official or {}).get("title") or f"Terminal-Bench {version}"
    lines = [f"### {title} (official)", ""]
    if official and official.get("rows"):
        lines += render_official_table(official, top)
    else:
        source = "committed snapshot" if offline_note else "live fetch"
        lines += [
            f"*No official leaderboard rows for Terminal-Bench {version} "
            f"right now ({source} returned none — the board may not exist "
            "yet or the hub may be unreachable). See the fa self-reported "
            "rows below and [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/).*",
        ]
    if fa_rows:
        lines += [
            "",
            f"#### fa on Terminal-Bench {version} — self-reported "
            f"{FA_MARKER} (not on the official leaderboard)",
            "",
        ] + render_fa_table(fa_rows, version)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def render_section(versions: "list[str]", official_by_version: "dict[str, dict]",
                   ledger: dict, top: int, offline_notes: "set[str]") -> str:
    fa_by_version = {}
    for row in ledger.get("results") or []:
        fa_by_version.setdefault(row.get("dataset_version"), []).append(row)
    for rows in fa_by_version.values():
        rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0))

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    parts = [
        SECTION_HEADER,
        "",
        "fa's own Terminal-Bench results next to the official field. "
        "Official rows are read from the Harbor Hub leaderboard that "
        "backs [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/); rows marked "
        f"{FA_MARKER} are **self-reported** — measured by our own "
        "bench-harbor runs, not submitted to the official board.",
        "",
        f"<sub>Regenerated {now} by "
        "`bench/leaderboard/render.py` (gh-1682).</sub>",
        "",
    ]
    for version in versions:
        parts.append(
            render_version_section(
                version, official_by_version.get(version),
                fa_by_version.get(version, []), top,
                version in offline_notes,
            )
        )
        parts.append("")
    return "\n".join(parts).rstrip() + "\n"


def splice_readme(text: str, section: str) -> str:
    """Replace the marked region (or insert before the anchor heading)."""
    begin = text.find(MARKER_BEGIN)
    end = text.find(MARKER_END)
    block = f"{MARKER_BEGIN}\n{section}{MARKER_END}\n"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fa results ledger upsert (gh-1682).

`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's OWN
Terminal-Bench results — the auto-update hook the leaderboard table
overlays on the official rows. It is written by the bench-harbor.yml
aggregate step on every completed run and by hand for backfills.

Usage (explicit fields):

    record.py --dataset-version 2.1 --model kimi-for-coding \
        --resolved 300 --total 445 --date 2026-10-18 \
        --fa-version 2fd100169e \
        --run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/3902812716 \
        [--run-url ...]

Usage (machine summary from summary.py --json-summary):

    record.py --summary /tmp/bench-summary.json

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (dataset_version, model) — one
aggregate row per dataset x model. Re-recording the same job (same
run_url) updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls; it never
appends a duplicate row. The 2.1 kimi row aggregates three workflow
runs (300/445 over runs 3902812716+39052822079+3909896789) exactly this
way.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool and the renderer leans on it for the honesty marker — never
blend fa rows into official leaderboard rows (gh-1682 AC2).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("fa_results.json")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    return (row.get("dataset_version", ""), row.get("model", ""))


def upsert(doc: dict, *, dataset_version: str, model: str, resolved: int,
           total: int, date: str, fa_version: str = None,
           run_urls: "list[str]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (dataset_version, model) row. Existing
    run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) so a job re-run updates
    instead of duplicating; numbers/date/fa_version reflect the latest
    record call."""
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (dataset_version, model):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"dataset_version": dataset_version, "model": model}
        doc["results"].append(row)
    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    row.update(
        {
            "resolved": int(resolved),
            "total": int(total),
            "date": date,
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-1682).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: dataset version desc, then accuracy desc (two
    # stable passes — one tuple with reverse=True would flip both keys).
    doc["results"].sort(
        key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0)
    )
    doc["results"].sort(key=lambda r: r.get("dataset_version", ""), reverse=True)
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="JSON totals from summary.py --json-summary")
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-version", dest="dataset_version")
    parser.add_argument("--model")
    parser.add_argument("--resolved", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--date")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.summary:
        summary = json.loads(args.summary.read_text())
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": summary.get("family"),
            "model": summary.get("model"),
            "resolved": summary.get("resolved"),
            "total": summary.get("total"),
            "date": summary.get("date"),
            "fa_version": summary.get("fa_ref"),
            "run_urls": [summary.get("run_url")] if summary.get("run_url") else [],
        }
        missing = [k for k, v in fields.items()
                   if v is None and k != "fa_version"]
        if missing:
            print(
                "::error::summary JSON is missing required field(s): "
                + ", ".join(missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
    else:
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": args.dataset_version,
            "model": args.model,
            "resolved": args.resolved,
            "total": args.total,
            "date": args.date,
            "fa_version": args.fa_version,
            "run_urls": args.run_urls,
        }
        missing = [k for k in ("dataset_version", "model", "resolved",
                               "total", "date")
                   if fields[k] is None]
        if missing:
            print(
                "error: missing required argument(s): "
                + ", ".join("--" + m.replace("_", "-") for m in missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

    doc = load_ledger(args.ledger)
    row = upsert(doc, **fields)
    save_ledger(doc, args.ledger)
    print(json.dumps(row, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1682: the leaderboard step commits the updated fa-results
    # ledger + regenerated README table back to the repo.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" \
            --json-summary leaderboard-summary.json jobs

      # gh-1682: auto-update the public leaderboard — append the run's
      # result to bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json (idempotent: keyed by
      # dataset version + model, run URLs union) and regenerate the
      # README table. Runs only on a COMPLETE full run (the verdict step
      # succeeded) — smoke/narrowed dispatches (non-empty tasks) never
      # touch the ledger.
      - name: Update leaderboard ledger & table
        if: success() && inputs.tasks == ''
        env:
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary leaderboard-summary.json
          # No --version: render every ledger version + the 4.0 field,
          # so the marked README block is rewritten whole, never shrunk
          # to the dispatch's single family.
          python bench/leaderboard/render.py
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "leaderboard: ledger and table already up to date"
          else
            git commit -m "bench: leaderboard ledger update · ${FAMILY} · ${MODEL} (gh-1682)"
            git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for the gh-1682 leaderboard tooling.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard

Hermetic: fetch-parse tests run against fixture captures (a real
tbench.ai page and a real Harbor Hub leaderboard-read response, both
captured 2026-10-18); no test touches the network.
"""
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import fetch
import record
import render

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURES = HERE / "fixtures"


def load_json(name: str) -> dict:
    return json.loads((FIXTURES / name).read_text())


class FetchHubParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_hub_fixture_normalizes(self):
        payload = load_json("hub_2-1_main.json")
        doc = fetch.normalize_hub_payload(payload, "2.1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["schema"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(doc["version"], "2.1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["source"], "harbor-hub")
        self.assertEqual(doc["package"], "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["leaderboard"], "main")
        rows = doc["rows"]
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), payload["pagination"]["total"])
        first = rows[0]
        # Sorted by accuracy desc, labels unwrapped from {label,url}.
        self.assertEqual(first["agent"], "Codex")
        self.assertEqual(first["model"], "GPT-6 Astra")
        self.assertEqual(first["agent_url"],
                         "https://openai.com/codex/")
        self.assertEqual(first["accuracy"], 87.42)
        self.assertEqual(first["n_trials"], 445)
        self.assertEqual(first["date"], "2026-09-03")
        accs = [r["accuracy"] for r in rows]
        self.assertEqual(accs, sorted(accs, reverse=True))

    def test_board_mapping_covers_all_families(self):
        for version in ("2.0", "2.1", "3.0", "4.0"):
            package, name = fetch.board_for(version)
            self.assertTrue(package.startswith("terminal-bench/"))
            self.assertTrue(name)
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
            fetch.board_for("9.9")


class FetchTbenchPageParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Parse the REAL captured tbench.ai page (Next.js RSC payloads) —
    never an HTML-table scrape."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.html = (FIXTURES / "tbench_ai_4-0-0.html").read_text()

    def test_extracts_dehydrated_rows(self):
        rows = fetch.parse_tbench_page(

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.ledger = Path(self.tmp.name) / "fa_results.json"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def _record(self, **kw):
        doc = record.load_ledger(self.ledger)
        row = record.upsert(doc, **kw)
        record.save_ledger(doc, self.ledger)
        return json.loads(self.ledger.read_text())

    def test_seed_rows(self):
        doc = self._record(
            dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",
            resolved=300, total=445, date="2026-10-18",
            fa_version="2fd100169e",
            run_urls=["https://x/actions/runs/1",
                      "https://x/actions/runs/2"])
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertTrue(row["self_reported"])
        self.assertEqual(row["resolved"], 300)
        self.assertEqual(len(row["run_urls"]), 2)

    def test_rerun_same_job_updates_not_duplicates(self):
        url = "https://x/actions/runs/39028127116"
        self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",
                     resolved=100, total=445, date="2026-10-17",
                     fa_version="a", run_urls=[url])
        doc = self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",
                           resolved=300, total=445, date="2026-10-18",
                           fa_version="b", run_urls=[url])
        self.assertEqual(len(doc["results"]), 1)
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["resolved"], 300)
        self.assertEqual(row["run_urls"], [url])  # deduped, not doubled
        self.assertEqual(row["fa_version"], "b")

    def test_multi_run_aggregate_unions_run_urls(self):
        # The 2.1 kimi seed: three workflow runs, one aggregate row.

                     resolved=140, total=200, date="2026-10-17",

        doc = self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",

            record.main(["--dataset-version", "2.1", "--model", "m"]),

# gh-1682: fa leaderboard — official tbench stats + self-reported fa results, auto-updated by bench runs

### What changed
New `bench/leaderboard/` tooling (stdlib-only python, same as the rest of bench/): `fetch.py` normalizes official Terminal-Bench leaderboard rows (model, agent, accuracy, date, source) for a dataset version, `record.py` upserts fa's own results into a committed `fa_results.json` ledger, and `render.py` merges both into a marked README section. The bench-harbor.yml summary job now appends the run's totals (new `--json-summary` in `summary.py`) to the ledger and re-renders + commits the table on every completed full run.

### Key decisions
- **Hub API first, tbench.ai fallback**: Harbor Hub `leaderboard-read` function (documented, backs tbench.ai); fallback parses the page's embedded Next.js RSC JSON (`self.__next_f.push`) — never HTML-table regex. Verified live mapping: 2.0→`terminal-bench-2/2-0`, 2.1→`terminal-bench-2-1/main`, 3.0/4.0→`terminal-bench/3-0-0`/`4-0-0`.
- **Honesty contract**: fa rows live in a separate table under a "self-reported ⭐ (not on the official leaderboard)" header with run links, fa version, and date; they never blend into official rows. Community submissions are closed (#1681) — noted in the footnote.
- **Ledger keyed by (dataset_version, model)**: re-running the same job unions run URLs and updates numbers in place — no duplicates (the 2.1 kimi row aggregates 3 workflow runs per the ticket). Seeded with the ticket's numbers (kimi 300/445 = 67.4%, GLM-5.3-flash 257/445 = 57.8%).
- **Committed snapshots** (`snapshots/<version>.json`) keep README regeneration reproducible; live fetch refreshes them and degrades to them when the hub is unreachable.
- Auto-update step is gated `success() && inputs.tasks == ''` — only complete full runs touch the ledger; smoke dispatches never do. Summary job gained `contents: write` for the commit.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard   # 21 tests, fixtures only (no network)
python3 bench/leaderboard/fetch.py --version 2.1     # normalized official rows JSON
python3 bench/leaderboard/render.py --check          # README table is fresh
```
Note: `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_usage.py` errors locally without the `harbor` pip package (CI installs `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`); pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

  SUM[summary.py --json-summary] --> REC[record.py]

# gh-1682: [GOAL] fa leaderboard table: fetch official tbench stats + overlay self-reported fa bench results, auto-updated by bench runs

## Description

### Goal

A visible, auto-updating **fa vs. the field** leaderboard table: pull the official Terminal-Bench stats (tbench.ai, `?version=2.1` today — Next.js app, data embedded in page JSON / backed by the Harbor hub API per docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/leaderboards), overlay fa's own bench results (we ran TB 2.0 earlier and 2.1 now), render a polished table for users.

### Design sketch (to be refined in implementation)

1. **Fetcher** (`bench/leaderboard/` script, python — same tooling as the rest of bench tooling): pull the official leaderboard rows for a given dataset version (2.0 / 2.1 / later 3.0/4.0 when they stabilize). Source of truth preference: Harbor hub API if it exposes leaderboard rows; fallback: parse tbench.ai's embedded page JSON. Never scrape HTML tables by regex — the page is Next.js with embedded structured data.
2. **fa rows source**: our own bench-harbor run summaries (`harbor-jobs-merged` artifact → summary.py accuracy) keyed by (dataset version, model, fa version, run url). A small committed ledger file (e.g. `bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json`) appended by the bench workflow on every completed run — that's the auto-update hook.
3. **Renderer**: Markdown table into `README.md` (between markers) and/or `docs/leaderboard.md` — rank by accuracy, fa rows highlighted. Honesty contract: fa rows are **self-reported, not on the official leaderboard** (community submissions are closed for 2.1/3.0/4.0 — see #1681) and must render with a visible marker + footnote (run date, fa version, dataset version, link to the GH run). Never blend self-reported rows visually with official rows.
4. **Auto-update**: bench-harbor.yml aggregate step appends the run's result to the ledger and regenerates the table (same commit as the run artifacts flow), so the table refreshes on every bench completion. Manual regeneration script for backfills.

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench/leaderboard/fetch.py --version 2.1` produces a normalized JSON of official rows (model, agent, accuracy, date, source url).
2. `fa_results.json` ledger + renderer: README section with the merged table, fa rows marked self-reported with run links.
3. bench-harbor.yml appends + re-renders on run completion (idempotent; a re-run of the same job updates, not duplicates).
4. Unit tests for fetch-parse (fixture HTML/JSON captured from tbench.ai) and merge/render logic.

### Context

- Official submissions are closed for TB 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 at the time of writing — this table is our public-facing evidence until #1681 (hub upload + ATIF) lets us submit officially.
- Latest fa numbers to seed the ledger: TB 2.1 kimi-for-coding 300/445 = 67.4% (runs 39028127116 + 39052822079 + 39098996789), GLM-5.3-flash 257/445 = 57.8% (run 38823577512).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Official Terminal-Bench leaderboard fetcher (gh-1682).

Usage:
    fetch.py --version 2.1 [--out rows.json] [--source auto|hub|tbench]

Pulls the official leaderboard rows for one Terminal-Bench dataset
version and prints a normalized JSON document:

    {
      "schema": 1,
      "version": "2.1",
      "package": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1",
      "leaderboard": "main",
      "title": "Terminal-Bench 2.1",
      "source": "harbor-hub" | "tbench.ai",
      "fetched_at": "<iso8601>",
      "rows": [
        {"rank": 1, "agent": "Codex", "agent_url": ...,
         "model": "GPT-6 Astra", "model_url": ...,
         "accuracy": 87.42, "n_trials": 445, "date": "2026-09-03",
         "cost_usd": ...},
        ...
      ]
    }

Source of truth (ticket order): the Harbor Hub API first — the public
`leaderboard-read` function documented at
docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/leaderboards and backing tbench.ai.
Fallback: parse tbench.ai's embedded page JSON (a Next.js app — the
leaderboard dehydrates into `self.__next_f.push` RSC payloads). HTML
tables are NEVER regex-scraped; only the embedded structured JSON is
read. `--source tbench` forces the fallback (used by tests/backfills).

Version -> (package, leaderboard name), verified live against the Hub
on 2026-10-18: the 2.x boards live under their own packages (only the
4.x/3.x generations share `terminal-bench/terminal-bench`):

    2.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2    2-0
    2.1  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1  main
    3.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      3-0-0
    4.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      4-0-0

Stdlib only (same tooling constraint as the rest of bench/).
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# version label -> (hub package, leaderboard name). Verified live against
# the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function (gh-1682).
BOARDS = {
    "2.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2", "2-0"),
    "2.1": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1", "main"),
    "3.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "3-0-0"),
    "4.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "4-0-0"),
}

HUB_READ_URL = "https://api.harborframework.com/functions/v1/leaderboard-read"
TBENCH_URL = "https://www.tbench.ai/"
# Hub row lists are paged; the docs example uses 100 and tbench.ai's own
# boards are a few dozen rows, so one page of 1000 covers a board whole.
HUB_PAGE_SIZE = 1000
HUB_MAX_PAGES = 20
HTTP_TIMEOUT = 30
USER_AGENT = "fa-leaderboard-fetch (gh-1682)"

# HTML tables are never scraped — only the Next.js RSC payload lines.
_RSC_PUSH_RE = re.compile(
    r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[1,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*\]\)'
)


def board_for(version: str) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    """Resolve a version label (or a bare board name under the 4.x
    package) to its (package, name); unknown versions fail loudly."""
    if version in BOARDS:
        return BOARDS[version]
    raise SystemExit(
        f"error: unknown Terminal-Bench version '{version}' — known boards: "
        + ", ".join(sorted(BOARDS))
    )


def _label(value) -> str:
    """Hub metadata fields are {'label': ..., 'url': ...} objects (or
    plain strings in older rows) — the table wants the label."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("label")
    return value


def _url(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("url")
    return None


def normalize_hub_payload(payload: dict, version: str) -> dict:
    """Normalize a leaderboard-read response body into our row schema."""
    lb = payload.get("leaderboard") or {}
    rows = []
    for row in payload.get("rows") or []:
        md = row.get("metadata") or {}
        mt = row.get("metrics") or {}
        rows.append(
            {
                "rank": row.get("rank"),
                "agent": _label(md.get("agent_display")),
                "agent_url": _url(md.get("agent_display")),
                "model": _label(md.get("model_display")),
                "model_url": _url(md.get("model_display")),
                "accuracy": mt.get("accuracy"),
                "n_trials": mt.get("n_trials"),
                "date": md.get("date"),

        "title": lb.get("title"),

        "source_url": HUB_READ_URL,
        "fetched_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "rows": rows,

def parse_tbench_page(html: str, package: str, name: str) -> list:
    """Extract one leaderboard's dehydrated rows from a tbench.ai page.

    tbench.ai is a Next.js app: the leaderboard query result dehydrates
    into `self.__next_f.push([1,"<json>"])` lines. We decode every such
    payload, find the query whose key is ["leaderboard", package, name],
    and return its data rows. Returns [] when the page does not carry
    that board (never an HTML-table fallback).
    """
    for raw in _RSC_PUSH_RE.findall(html):
        # The captured group is a JSON string literal — json.loads
        # decodes both \" and \uXXXX correctly (unicode_escape would
        # mangle multi-byte labels).
        try:
            text = json.loads('"' + raw + '"')
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        start = text.find("{")
        if start < 0:

        try:
            payload, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[start:])
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        queries = (payload.get("state") or {}).get("queries") or []
        for query in queries:
            if query.get("queryKey") != ["leaderboard", package, name]:
                continue
            data = (query.get("state") or {}).get("data") or {}
            return list(data.get("rows") or [])
    return []

    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())


def _http_get(url: str) -> str:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Leaderboard renderer: merge official rows + fa self-reported rows into
the README table (gh-1682).

Usage:
    render.py [--version 2.1]... [--top 15] [--offline] [--readme README.md]

Renders one subsection per dataset version into the marked region of
README.md:

    <!-- leaderboard:begin -->
    ...generated...
    <!-- leaderboard:end -->

Honesty contract (gh-1682 AC2): official rows and fa rows live in
SEPARATE tables under separate headers — fa rows carry a ⭐ marker, the
"self-reported, not on the official leaderboard" label, and a footnote
with run date, fa version, dataset version, and the GitHub run link(s).
They are never sorted into or styled like official rows.

Official rows come from fetch.py (Harbor Hub API -> tbench.ai page-JSON
fallback). `--offline` reads the committed snapshots instead — the
snapshots keep README regeneration reproducible and let the auto-update
step degrade to the last captured board instead of failing when the hub
is unreachable. A version with no official rows and no snapshot renders
an explicit "no official rows" note — never an empty table that could
read as an empty field.

Regenerating with unchanged inputs leaves README.md untouched (the
workflow's commit step relies on that for idempotency).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import fetch
import record

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
README_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "README.md"
SNAPSHOT_DIR = HERE / "snapshots"

MARKER_BEGIN = "<!-- leaderboard:begin (gh-1682) -->"
MARKER_END = "<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->"
INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING = "## What's inside"
# README section header lives inside the marked region, so removing the
# markers removes the whole section.
SECTION_HEADER = "## Leaderboard: fa vs. the field"
FA_MARKER = "⭐"

DEFAULT_OFFICIAL_VERSIONS = ("4.0",)


def pct(part: int, total: int) -> str:
    return f"{100.0 * part / total:.1f}%" if total else "n/a"


def _link(label: str, url: str) -> str:
    return f"[{label}]({url})" if url else label


def _run_link(url: str) -> str:
    """A GitHub Actions run URL renders by its run id (the stable,
    auditable handle) — full URLs in every cell would drown the table."""
    run_id = url.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return _link(run_id, url)


def render_official_table(doc: dict, top: int) -> "list[str]":
    rows = doc.get("rows") or []
    shown = rows[:top]
    lines = [
        "| # | Agent | Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for i, r in enumerate(shown, 1):
        lines.append(
            "| {rank} | {agent} | {model} | {acc} | {n} | {date} |".format(
                rank=r.get("rank") or i,
                agent=_link(r["agent"], r.get("agent_url")) or "—",
                model=_link(r["model"], r.get("model_url")) or "—",
                acc=pct_1(r.get("accuracy")),
                n=r.get("n_trials") or "—",
                date=r.get("date") or "—",
            )
        )
    fetched = (doc.get("fetched_at") or "")[:10]
    note = (
        f"Official rows: Harbor Hub leaderboard "
        f"`{doc.get('package')}/{doc.get('leaderboard')}` — "
        f"backing [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/)"
    )
    if len(rows) > len(shown):
        note += f", top {len(shown)} of {len(rows)}"
    if fetched:
        note += f", fetched {fetched}"
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"<sub>{note}.</sub>")
    return lines


def pct_1(accuracy) -> str:
    """Hub accuracy is a 0-100 percentage; render one decimal."""
    if accuracy is None:
        return "n/a"
    return f"{float(accuracy):.1f}%"


def render_fa_table(rows: "list[dict]", version: str) -> "list[str]":
    lines = [
        "| Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date | fa | Runs |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in rows:
        runs = " + ".join(_run_link(u) for u in r.get("run_urls") or []) or "—"
        fa = r.get("fa_version") or "—"
        lines.append(
            f"| {FA_MARKER} {r.get('model', '—')} "
            f"| {pct(r.get('resolved', 0), r.get('total', 0))} "
            f"| {r.get('resolved', '—')}/{r.get('total', '—')} "
            f"| {r.get('date', '—')} "
            f"| `{fa}` "
            f"| {runs} |"
        )
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        f"<sub>{FA_MARKER} Self-reported: measured by our own "
        f"`bench-harbor` runs on Terminal-Bench {version}, **not** an "
        "official leaderboard submission (community submissions are "
        "closed — #1681). Every row links its GitHub Actions run(s); fa "
        "rows never blend into the official table above. Source: "
        "`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json`.</sub>"
    )
    return lines


def render_version_section(version: str, official: dict,
                           fa_rows: "list[dict]", top: int,
                           offline_note: bool) -> str:
    title = (official or {}).get("title") or f"Terminal-Bench {version}"
    lines = [f"### {title} (official)", ""]
    if official and official.get("rows"):
        lines += render_official_table(official, top)
    else:
        source = "committed snapshot" if offline_note else "live fetch"
        lines += [
            f"*No official leaderboard rows for Terminal-Bench {version} "
            f"right now ({source} returned none — the board may not exist "
            "yet or the hub may be unreachable). See the fa self-reported "
            "rows below and [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/).*",
        ]
    if fa_rows:
        lines += [
            "",
            f"#### fa on Terminal-Bench {version} — self-reported "
            f"{FA_MARKER} (not on the official leaderboard)",
            "",
        ] + render_fa_table(fa_rows, version)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def render_section(versions: "list[str]", official_by_version: "dict[str, dict]",
                   ledger: dict, top: int, offline_notes: "set[str]") -> str:
    fa_by_version = {}
    for row in ledger.get("results") or []:
        fa_by_version.setdefault(row.get("dataset_version"), []).append(row)
    for rows in fa_by_version.values():
        rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0))

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    parts = [
        SECTION_HEADER,
        "",
        "fa's own Terminal-Bench results next to the official field. "
        "Official rows are read from the Harbor Hub leaderboard that "
        "backs [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/); rows marked "
        f"{FA_MARKER} are **self-reported** — measured by our own "
        "bench-harbor runs, not submitted to the official board.",
        "",
        f"<sub>Regenerated {now} by "
        "`bench/leaderboard/render.py` (gh-1682).</sub>",
        "",
    ]
    for version in versions:
        parts.append(
            render_version_section(
                version, official_by_version.get(version),
                fa_by_version.get(version, []), top,
                version in offline_notes,
            )
        )
        parts.append("")
    return "\n".join(parts).rstrip() + "\n"


def splice_readme(text: str, section: str) -> str:
    """Replace the marked region (or insert before the anchor heading)."""
    begin = text.find(MARKER_BEGIN)
    end = text.find(MARKER_END)
    block = f"{MARKER_BEGIN}\n{section}{MARKER_END}\n"
    if begin >= 0 and end > begin:
        return text[:begin] + block + text[end + len(MARKER_END) + 1:]
    anchor = text.find(INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING)
    if anchor < 0:
        return text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + block
    return text[:anchor] + block + "\n" + text[anchor:]

    """Refresh the committed snapshot after a successful live fetch.

    `fetched_at` is preserved when the board itself is unchanged, so a

    commit step only picks up real changes.
    """

    snap = SNAPSHOT_DIR / f"{version}.json"
    new = dict(doc)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fa results ledger upsert (gh-1682).

`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's OWN
Terminal-Bench results — the auto-update hook the leaderboard table
overlays on the official rows. It is written by the bench-harbor.yml
aggregate step on every completed run and by hand for backfills.

Usage (explicit fields):

    record.py --dataset-version 2.1 --model kimi-for-coding \
        --resolved 300 --total 445 --date 2026-10-18 \
        --fa-version 2fd100169e \
        --run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/3902812716 \
        [--run-url ...]

Usage (machine summary from summary.py --json-summary):

    record.py --summary /tmp/bench-summary.json

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (dataset_version, model) — one
aggregate row per dataset x model. Re-recording the same job (same
run_url) updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls; it never
appends a duplicate row. The 2.1 kimi row aggregates three workflow
runs (300/445 over runs 3902812716+39052822079+3909896789) exactly this
way.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool and the renderer leans on it for the honesty marker — never
blend fa rows into official leaderboard rows (gh-1682 AC2).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("fa_results.json")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    return (row.get("dataset_version", ""), row.get("model", ""))


def upsert(doc: dict, *, dataset_version: str, model: str, resolved: int,
           total: int, date: str, fa_version: str = None,
           run_urls: "list[str]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (dataset_version, model) row. Existing
    run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) so a job re-run updates
    instead of duplicating; numbers/date/fa_version reflect the latest
    record call."""
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (dataset_version, model):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"dataset_version": dataset_version, "model": model}
        doc["results"].append(row)
    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    row.update(
        {
            "resolved": int(resolved),
            "total": int(total),
            "date": date,
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-1682).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: dataset version desc, then accuracy desc (two
    # stable passes — one tuple with reverse=True would flip both keys).
    doc["results"].sort(
        key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0)
    )
    doc["results"].sort(key=lambda r: r.get("dataset_version", ""), reverse=True)
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="JSON totals from summary.py --json-summary")
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-version", dest="dataset_version")
    parser.add_argument("--model")
    parser.add_argument("--resolved", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--date")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.summary:
        summary = json.loads(args.summary.read_text())
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": summary.get("family"),
            "model": summary.get("model"),
            "resolved": summary.get("resolved"),
            "total": summary.get("total"),
            "date": summary.get("date"),
            "fa_version": summary.get("fa_ref"),
            "run_urls": [summary.get("run_url")] if summary.get("run_url") else [],
        }
        missing = [k for k, v in fields.items()
                   if v is None and k != "fa_version"]
        if missing:
            print(
                "::error::summary JSON is missing required field(s): "
                + ", ".join(missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
    else:
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": args.dataset_version,
            "model": args.model,
            "resolved": args.resolved,
            "total": args.total,
            "date": args.date,
            "fa_version": args.fa_version,
            "run_urls": args.run_urls,
        }
        missing = [k for k in ("dataset_version", "model", "resolved",
                               "total", "date")
                   if fields[k] is None]
        if missing:
            print(
                "error: missing required argument(s): "
                + ", ".join("--" + m.replace("_", "-") for m in missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

    doc = load_ledger(args.ledger)
    row = upsert(doc, **fields)
    save_ledger(doc, args.ledger)
    print(json.dumps(row, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

|| echo "::warning::${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1682: the leaderboard step commits the updated fa-results
    # ledger + regenerated README table back to the repo.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" \
            --json-summary leaderboard-summary.json jobs

      # gh-1682: auto-update the public leaderboard — append the run's
      # result to bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json (idempotent: keyed by
      # dataset version + model, run URLs union) and regenerate the
      # README table. Runs only on a COMPLETE full run (the verdict step
      # succeeded) — smoke/narrowed dispatches (non-empty tasks) never
      # touch the ledger.
      - name: Update leaderboard ledger & table
        if: success() && inputs.tasks == ''
        env:
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary leaderboard-summary.json
          # No --version: render every ledger version + the 4.0 field,
          # so the marked README block is rewritten whole, never shrunk
          # to the dispatch's single family.
          python bench/leaderboard/render.py
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard

class FetchHubParseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_hub_fixture_normalizes(self):
        payload = load_json("hub_2-1_main.json")
        doc = fetch.normalize_hub_payload(payload, "2.1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["schema"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(doc["version"], "2.1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["source"], "harbor-hub")
        self.assertEqual(doc["package"], "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1")
        self.assertEqual(doc["leaderboard"], "main")
        rows = doc["rows"]
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), payload["pagination"]["total"])
        first = rows[0]
        # Sorted by accuracy desc, labels unwrapped from {label,url}.
        self.assertEqual(first["agent"], "Codex")
        self.assertEqual(first["model"], "GPT-6 Astra")
        self.assertEqual(first["agent_url"],
                         "https://openai.com/codex/")
        self.assertEqual(first["accuracy"], 87.42)
        self.assertEqual(first["n_trials"], 445)
        self.assertEqual(first["date"], "2026-09-03")
        accs = [r["accuracy"] for r in rows]
        self.assertEqual(accs, sorted(accs, reverse=True))

    def test_board_mapping_covers_all_families(self):
        for version in ("2.0", "2.1", "3.0", "4.0"):

            self.assertTrue(package.startswith("terminal-bench/"))
            self.assertTrue(name)
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):

class RecordTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.ledger = Path(self.tmp.name) / "fa_results.json"

    def tearDown(self):

    def _record(self, **kw):
        doc = record.load_ledger(self.ledger)

        return json.loads(self.ledger.read_text())

    def test_seed_rows(self):
        doc = self._record(
            dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",
            resolved=300, total=445, date="2026-10-18",
            fa_version="2fd100169e",
            run_urls=["https://x/actions/runs/1",

        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertTrue(row["self_reported"])
        self.assertEqual(row["resolved"], 300)
        self.assertEqual(len(row["run_urls"]), 2)

    def test_rerun_same_job_updates_not_duplicates(self):
        url = "https://x/actions/runs/39028127116"
        self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",
                     resolved=100, total=445, date="2026-10-17",

        self.assertEqual(len(doc["results"]), 1)

        self.assertEqual(row["resolved"], 300)
        self.assertEqual(row["run_urls"], [url])  # deduped, not doubled

        self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",

                     run_urls=["https://x/actions/runs/1"])
        doc = self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",

        self.assertEqual(doc["results"][0]["run_urls"], [

    def test_sorted_by_version_then_accuracy(self):
        doc = self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="glm-5.3-flash",

                           run_urls=[])
        doc = self._record(dataset_version="2.1", model="kimi-for-coding",
